candidates.title: Mitochondria-targeted ROS-scavenging nanoreactor with dual-drug-loaded carbon dots for osteoarthritis therapy.
candidates.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) pathology entails complex interactions among oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, cartilage degradation, and dysregulation of subchondral bone remodeling. Current therapeutic agents suffer from limited efficacy due to poor joint targeting and low bioavailability, highlighting the critical need for advanced drug delivery systems. In this study, a mitochondria-targeting reactive oxygen species (ROS)-scavenging nanoreactor (A@HP@SH/T) was developed for multi-mechanism OA repair. The nanoreactor is constructed using hollow mesoporous prussian blue (HMPB) as the carrier, loaded with carbon dots (AA CDs) co-assembled from astragaloside IV (AS-IV) and alendronate sodium (ALN), coated with diselenide-modified hyaluronic acid (Se-Se HA), and further conjugated with the mitochondrial-targeting ligand TPP. Through a temporal cascade of TPP-mediated mitochondrial anchoring, Se-Se HA ROS-responsive cleavage, and HMPB-mediated in situ protection and sustained release, AA CDs are precisely delivered to the lesion site, where they efficiently scavenge ROS and modulate mitochondrial homeostasis, thereby fundamentally breaking the vicious cycle of oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and cartilage degradation within the joint. Additionally, the ALN component in AA CDs targets subchondral bone and modulates bone metabolism to reshape the local microstructure, offering both mechanical support and a beneficial nutritional microenvironment for cartilage regeneration. Both in vitro and in vivo studies confirmed that this system effectively restores mitochondrial homeostasis, alleviates inflammation, promotes cartilage differentiation, and regulates bone metabolism, thereby promoting OA repair. Collectively, this nanoreactor represents a highly promising strategy for the treatment of osteoarthritis.

candidates.title: Primary adrenal small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma in a patient with sarcoidosis and synchronous colon adenocarcinoma.
candidates.abstract: Primary adrenal neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC), particularly the small cell subtype, is exceptionally rare. In patients with sarcoidosis, inflammatory lymphadenopathy may mimic a metastatic disease, making disease detection difficult. A 76-year-old man with sarcoidosis was referred for an enlarging left adrenal incidentaloma that had increased in size from 7 mm to 19 × 14 mm over 3 years. Hormonal evaluation revealed unremarkable findings; laparoscopic adrenalectomy was performed because malignancy could not be excluded. Histopathological examination revealed small cell NEC with positive synaptophysin and chromogranin A staining, and a Ki-67 labeling index of 80%. One month after surgery, para-aortic lymphadenopathy was detected. Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (CT) showed uptake in the para-aortic lymph nodes and ascending colon, where colonoscopy identified synchronous adenocarcinoma. The cause of the lymphadenopathy was uncertain because of coexisting sarcoidosis and colon cancer. Cisplatin plus irinotecan induced a partial response; however, disease progression was observed. CT-guided lymph node biopsy confirmed metastatic NEC. Second-line amrubicin therapy reduced tumor size; comprehensive genomic profiling revealed a tumor mutation-burden-high phenotype. This case highlights diagnostic challenges in the evaluation of lymphadenopathy in patients with sarcoidosis and synchronous malignancy, emphasizing the importance of pathological confirmation for guiding appropriate management.

candidates.title: Effectiveness and Safety of a Moisturizer Containing Centella Asiatica Extract, Ceramide NP, and Panthenol for Erythema and Skin Barrier in Erythematotelangiectatic Rosacea: A Randomized Controlled Trial Study.
candidates.abstract: Erythematotelangiectatic rosacea is a chronic recurrent inflammatory disease that often impose a significant psychological burden on patients. Given that effective moisturization is integral to its management, the choice of a proper moisturizer is a critical clinical consideration. Our study aims to assess the effectiveness and safety of a moisturizer containing Centella asiatica extract, ceramide NP, and panthenol for erythema and skin barrier in Chinese patients with erythematotelangiectatic rosacea. All enrolled patients were prescribed oral minocycline 50 mg once daily and applied moisturizer twice daily. Facial images of facial redness, stratum corneum hydration (SCH), transepidermal water loss (TEWL), and Clinician's Erythema Assessment (CEA) were collected at baseline, day 7 (D7), day 14 (D14), and day 28 (D28). Time to a 1-point reduction in the Patient's Self-Assessment (PSA) scale and Rosacea-specific Quality-of-life instrument (RosQol) were also recorded by patients. A total of 75 patients with rosacea were enrolled, 39 patients were randomized to the experimental group and 36 to the control group. Our study showed that the variations of a* value, facial red area, SCH and RosQol from baseline to D28 were rapidly and significantly greater in the experimental group, and the mean rank of CEA was significantly higher in the control group at D28. All AEs were mild and self-limiting. This study found that the moisturizer containing Centella asiatica extract, ceramide NP, and panthenol delivers rapid, effective adjunctive benefits in rosacea treatment and represents a reliable daily skincare option for patients.
candidates.journal: Skin research and technology : official journal of International Society for Bioengineering and the Skin (ISBS) [and] International Society for Digital Imaging of Skin (ISDIS) [and] International Society for Skin Imaging (ISSI)

candidates.title: Scientific and Regulatory Policy Committee Points to Consider: Virtual Control Groups and Their Implications for Anatomic and Clinical Pathology Evaluation During Nonclinical Toxicity Studies.
candidates.abstract: Replacement of concurrent control groups (CCG) with virtual control groups (VCG) has been advocated as a strategy to reduce animal use in nonclinical toxicity testing. This "Points to Consider" paper examines VCG utility as it impacts toxicologic pathology endpoints and identifies the following points. (1) The CCG remains the gold standard, as it best controls for extrinsic and intrinsic study variables in discriminating subtle effects. (2) Pure VCG are unlikely to provide the same discernment since historical control data (HCD) from which VCG are assembled do not share all biological, environmental, husbandry, and procedural attributes of animals in the current study. (3) Clinical pathology endpoints are particularly vulnerable to VCG distortion given their dynamic range and sensitivity to preanalytical variables, with proof-of-concept studies demonstrating nonreproducibility rates for data interpretation of 31% to 49%. (4) Hybrid control groups combining reduced CCG with VCG are the most rational implementation strategy, balancing 3Rs (reduction, refinement, replacement) goals with scientific rigor and ongoing HCD refreshment. (5) The HCD pools require major upgrades, including comprehensive individual animal metadata, particularly for preanalytical and analytical variables, and (6) access to archived tissues as whole-slide scanned images, permitting reevaluation by the study pathologist using consistent nomenclature and grading criteria. (7) No major regulatory authority currently accepts VCG as a replacement for CCG in Good Laboratory Practice studies, and (8) proprietary data and data-sharing barriers to building sufficiently large multi-institutional HCD databases remain unresolved. (9) The VCG feasibility is highly species-dependent. (10) Multiple other new approach methodologies and modified study designs can support reduced animal use when VCG are not an optimal approach.

candidates.title: Hyperphagia in Prader-Willi syndrome: linking hypothalamic dysfunction to clinical assessment and management across the lifespan.
candidates.abstract: Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) is a rare genetic neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by hypothalamic dysfunction and profound dysregulation in hunger and appetite regulation, endocrine function, metabolism and behaviour. Hyperphagia is a defining clinical feature and a major contributor to morbidity, mortality and caregiver burden. Increasing evidence suggests that hyperphagia in PWS represents a multidimensional disorder rather than excessive appetite alone. In December 2024, an international meeting of clinical and scientific experts was convened in Toulouse, France, to explore current understanding of hyperphagia in PWS, challenges in assessment, and evolving approaches to management across the lifespan. Although not a formal consensus process, several consistent themes emerged. These included limitations of existing assessment tools, the need for multidimensional evaluation (including use of instruments such as the Hyperphagia Questionnaire and Hyperphagia Questionnaire for Clinical Trials (HQ-CT). The central role of structured food environments, and vulnerabilities during transition to adult care were also identified as key themes. Experts emphasised that hyperphagia reflects interactions between impaired satiety signalling, activation in reward neurocircuitry, autonomic dysfunction and environmental factors. Management therefore requires integrated biological, behavioural and environmental approaches. While food security and structured support remain foundational, emerging pharmacological therapies may complement multidisciplinary care and reduce caregiver burden. Hyperphagia in PWS should be conceptualised as a complex, multidimensional disorder requiring comprehensive assessment and integrated management. Future priorities include development of additional validated outcome measures, identification of biomarkers, and care models that better align mechanistic insights with real-world clinical practice.

candidates.title: In Vitro and In Vivo Characterization of Porcine Urothelial Cells as an Intravesical Cellular Xenotransplantation Immunotherapeutic Agent for Bladder Cancer.
candidates.abstract: Cellular xenotransplantation offers a unique immunotherapeutic strategy for cancer by utilizing xenogeneic cells to elicit robust host immune responses. Innovative treatments are required for non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) due to the limited effectiveness of current standard therapies. Intravesical xenogeneic porcine urothelial cell (PUC) immunotherapy provides a novel mechanism-of-action option. This study evaluates cellular xenotransplantation utilizing primary PUCs in vitro and in vivo to characterize their potential as an intravesical immunotherapeutic agent for NMIBC. Primary PUC phenotypic and transcriptomic identities were first characterized using flow cytometry and bulk RNA sequencing. Subsequently, the effects of basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF) and the ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 on PUC expansion capacity, gene expression, and senescence were investigated. Immune-stimulatory potency was measured through cell-based co-culture bioassays, and in vivo biodistribution and immune recruitment were assessed in mice following intravesical instillation. Expanded PUCs demonstrated high epithelial purity (92.16% ± 5.38% CD49f+). RNA-seq profiles confirmed a distinct urothelial identity (e.g., UPK3A, TP63, KRT7), with unsupervised clustering clearly separating PUCs from skeletal muscle comparators. Combined treatment with bFGF and Y-27632 synergistically promoted growth and upregulated differentiation markers while significantly suppressing p16-mediated senescence. PUCs significantly stimulated immune cell proliferation and IFN-γ/IL-2 secretion through direct, F-actin-polarized interactions. in vivo, PUCs remained localized and were cleared within 28 days, inducing a peak recruitment of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells at Day 14 and enhancing systemic cytotoxicity. PUCs serve as a potent, localized, and transient cellular medicine that primes systemic antitumor-like immunity. The optimized expansion protocol facilitates the scalable production of non-senescent porcine cells for clinical applications in bladder cancer.

candidates.title: Acinetobacter baumannii Nosocomial Meningitis Secondary to Neurosurgical Intervention: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Nosocomial meningitis is a serious complication of neurosurgical procedures, associated with high morbidity and mortality, as well as significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Among the causative pathogens, Acinetobacter baumannii (A. baumannii) is particularly concerning due to its ability to survive for prolonged periods in the hospital environment, its opportunistic virulence, and, especially, its tendency to develop multidrug resistance to antimicrobial agents. Diagnosis is often difficult in the postoperative setting, particularly when the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is altered as a result of the surgical procedure. Rapid identification of the causative agent and early initiation of appropriate antibiotic therapy are essential to limit complications and improve patient prognosis. We report the case of a 27-year-old patient with a history of surgically treated craniopharyngioma complicated by anterior hypopituitarism. Three weeks after surgery, he was admitted to the ICU with suspected postoperative meningitis due to the onset of behavioral disturbances associated with nasal discharge, without a fever. Brain CT was normal. CSF analysis, obtained by lumbar puncture under strict aseptic conditions, revealed a turbid fluid with leukocytosis of 5,760 cells/mm³, predominantly composed of neutrophils, along with elevated protein levels (5.7 g/L) and low glucose levels (0.05 g/L). Direct examination after Gram staining showed Gram-negative coccobacilli with a marked inflammatory reaction. CSF culture grew a multidrug-resistant (MDR) strain of A. baumannii, which was sensitive only to colistin. The patient received antibiotic therapy with colistin, administered intravenously and intrathecally for 18 days, with initial neurological improvement and sterilization of the CSF by the 15th day of treatment. The subsequent course was unfavorable, marked by the development of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) secondary to ventilator-associated pneumonia caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), complicated by refractory septic shock, which ultimately led to his death after one month of hospitalization in the ICU. This report highlights the severity of nosocomial meningitis caused by MDR A. baumannii and underscores the importance of implementing infection prevention measures in healthcare settings.

candidates.title: Medullary thyroid carcinoma with pheochromocytoma and cystic parathyroid degeneration in a ret-negative patient: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A (MEN2A) is a rare autosomal dominant hereditary cancer syndrome, predominantly caused by mutations of the RET proto-oncogene on chromosome 10q11.2. It typically presents with medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), pheochromocytoma, and primary hyperparathyroidism. Cases with a MEN2A phenotype but negative RET testing are uncommon, posing challenges for diagnosis and patient management. We report the case of a 63-year-old female who was diagnosed with MTC and pheochromocytoma. and cystic parathyroid gland. Genetic workup was negative for RET proto-oncogene mutations but positive for a heterozygous variant in the TMEM127 tumor suppressor gene. MEN2A is associated with pathogenic germline variants in the RET proto-oncogene in approximately 95-99% of cases. Our patient, however, exhibited a MEN2A-like clinical phenotype in the absence of an identifiable RET mutation, with a pathogenic TMEM127 variant instead. Although TMEM127 is an established susceptibility gene for pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma, its association with the broader MEN2A phenotype remains unclear. This unusual genotype-phenotype discordance raises important questions regarding the potential role of alternative genetic pathways in MEN2-like syndromes and creates uncertainty regarding postoperative surveillance and the appropriate extent of screening and genetic counseling for family members. Our case represents an unusual scenario where the patient presents with a clinical phenotype of MEN2A but is RET negative and positive heterozygous for a variant in the TMEM127. This atypical genetic finding introduces complexities in determining the appropriate follow-up protocol and the scope of familial screening necessary.

candidates.title: A Clinical Insight into Von Hippel-Lindau Syndrome: Diagnostic Challenges.
candidates.abstract: Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) syndrome is a rare hereditary disorder characterised by the development of multiple benign and malignant tumours across various organs. Caused by mutations in the VHL tumour suppressor gene, it presents a wide range of clinical manifestations, including retinal haemangioblastomas, central nervous system tumours, renal cell carcinoma, pancreatic lesions, and phaeochromocytomas. This report describes the case of a 35-year-old woman who presented with visual impairment and abdominal masses. Imaging revealed typical VHL manifestations, including bilateral renal lesions and pancreatic involvement. Genetic testing confirmed the diagnosis. The patient underwent staged partial nephrectomies, with histopathology confirming clear cell renal cell carcinoma in both kidneys. This case highlights the importance of recognising the variable clinical and radiological presentations of VHL syndrome. Early diagnosis and multidisciplinary management are essential to reduce morbidity and mortality. Increased awareness and regular surveillance are critical for timely detection and intervention in patients with VHL syndrome.

candidates.title: The Effect of Digital Storytelling on the Anxiety of Patients with Pituitary Adenoma Undergoing Transsphenoidal Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
candidates.abstract: Patients with pituitary adenoma often experience anxiety due to hormonal changes and the stress associated with transsphenoidal surgery. Digital storytelling, as an innovative multimedia-based training method, has recently been used in patient education. This study investigated the effect of digital storytelling on the anxiety of patients with pituitary adenoma undergoing transsphenoidal surgery. This randomized controlled trial was conducted on 70 patients with pituitary adenoma scheduled for transsphenoidal surgery at a teaching hospital affiliated with Tehran University of Medical Sciences. Participants were randomly assigned to an intervention or a control group. The intervention group received a 15-20-minute digital storytelling program that included experiences shared by patients and nurses regarding preoperative and postoperative care, while the control group received routine hospital education. Anxiety levels were measured a day before surgery, a day after surgery, and three weeks later using Spielberger's State Anxiety Scale. Data were analyzed by SPSS-25 software using descriptive and inferential statistics. The mean score of anxiety in the intervention group decreased by 12.45 (1.24) units a day after the surgery and by 24.82 (1.32) units three weeks after the surgery compared to baseline (p < 0.001). A significantly lower anxiety level was observed in the intervention group at both post-intervention time periods compared to the pre-intervention time (F = 17.05, p < 0.001). Repeated measures Analysis of Variance confirmed a significant interaction between time and group (F = 25.31, p < 0.001). Digital storytelling was effective in reducing anxiety among patients with pituitary adenoma undergoing transsphenoidal surgery and may serve as a valuable educational intervention.
candidates.journal: Iranian journal of nursing and midwifery research

candidates.title: Case Report: Veno-Arteriovenous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation for Management of Pheochromocytoma-Induced Cardiac Arrest in a Post-Partum Patient.
candidates.abstract: A 34-year-old woman, 2 days post-partum, was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) for management of hypertensive crisis and respiratory failure. An 18-cm left adrenal mass was found on computed tomography (CT), suspicious for a pheochromocytoma. After cardiac arrest, the patient was placed on veno-arteriovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (V-AV ECMO) given recurrent destabilizing arrhythmias. After successful ECMO decannulation, the patient underwent an uncomplicated resection of her adrenal mass. Although VA-ECMO has been used to support patients with pheochromocytoma, this appears to be the first published case describing the use of a V-AV configuration in the management of a complex cardiac arrest.

candidates.title: A Modified Delphi Process to Identify Clinical and Research Priorities for Aging Transgender Adults.
candidates.abstract: Aging transgender adults experience unique medical and social challenges, but limited data exist regarding healthcare needs and priorities. Identifying these can help guide transgender-informed, patient-centered care and aging research. We employed a modified, two-round Delphi method with a consensus committee to identify clinical and research priorities for aging transgender adults. Expert panelists with experience in transgender, geriatric, and/or HIV care and research rated 15 clinical and 7 research topics using a 5-point Likert scale. Consensus was defined as > 80% of expert panelists ranking a topic as "Very important" or "Extremely important." Following Round 1, a consensus committee of older transgender adults reviewed topics and write-in suggestions and could elevate, reinstate, or add priorities by unanimous agreement. Topics selected by the committee advanced to Round 2 for expert panel ranking, followed by consensus committee review. Forty-eight expert panelists completed Round 1, and 31 completed Round 2. After Round 1, 11 clinical and 3 research topics reached consensus. Following consensus committee review, 10 clinical and 6 research priorities advanced to Round 2. After final review, the highest-ranked clinical priorities were "Provider knowledge on the unique needs of older transgender adults," "Evaluation of social isolation, loneliness, and social support networks," and "Provider/clinic knowledge of social, legal, financial, and mental health resources for transgender persons." The highest-ranked research priorities were "Clinical implications of long-term gender-affirming hormone therapy and hormone cessation," "Biologic mechanisms of hormone therapy on aging and aging outcomes," and "Health, social, and structural needs of older transgender persons." Using a community-engaged modified Delphi approach, this study identified key clinical and research priorities for older transgender adults. Findings highlight the importance of provider knowledge, social support, and addressing knowledge gaps in gender-affirming care and aging. These results provide direction for future research and best practice guidelines for this population.
candidates.journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society

candidates.title: Complex cardiac overlap: immune checkpoint inhibitor myocarditis in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy with subsequent NSTEMI.
candidates.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myocarditis is a rare but life-threatening complication, particularly challenging to diagnose in patients with coexisting cardiac conditions. A 58-year-old man with advanced oropharyngeal carcinoma treated with pembrolizumab presented with heart failure symptoms and markedly elevated troponin levels. Imaging revealed hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) alongside cardiac magnetic resonance findings consistent with ICI-associated myocarditis. He initially responded to high-dose corticosteroids but relapsed due to non-adherence, requiring re-treatment and addition of mycophenolate mofetil. Following recovery, he developed a significant rise in troponin with new regional wall motion abnormalities. Coronary angiography demonstrated significant coronary artery disease, supporting the diagnosis of acute coronary syndrome in the context of the clinical presentation, biomarker elevation, and imaging findings, managed with percutaneous coronary intervention. Post-procedural hypotension was attributed to adrenal insufficiency and resolved with stress-dose corticosteroids. Follow-up imaging demonstrated features of both prior myocarditis and new ischemic injury. The patient improved clinically after PCI and was discharged with normalized troponin levels. This case highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges of ICI-associated myocarditis in the presence of overlapping cardiac pathologies. Multimodality imaging and clinical context are essential for accurate diagnosis, and alternative causes of troponin elevation must be carefully excluded.

candidates.title: A Self-Adaptive CoNi-Based Metal-Organic Framework for Autonomous Antibacterial Efficacy and Anti-Inflammatory Resolution in Accelerated Wound Healing.
candidates.abstract: Delayed healing of bacterially infected wounds stems from drug-resistant bacterial invasion and excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS)-driven inflammation, which necessitating strategies that simultaneously eradicate pathogens and resolve inflammation. We designed a bimetallic CoNi-based metal-organic framework (CoNi-MOF) with enhanced multienzyme-like activities: oxidase-like (OXD-like), peroxidase-like (POD-like), and catalase-like (CAT-like) activities. The superior performance arises from the synergy between Co and Ni, which shifts the d-band center of Co closer to the Fermi level than those in Co-MOF and Ni-MOF. This electronic structure enhancement facilitates substrate adsorption and lowers reaction energy barriers, accounting for the strong enzyme-like activities of CoNi-MOF. At acidic infection sites, OXD-like and POD-like activities are activated to generate antibacterial ROS, effectively eliminating drug-resistant bacteria. As bacterial clearance occurs and the wound returns to neutrality, CoNi-MOF exhibits CAT-like activity and radical scavenging capabilities to eliminate excess ROS, thereby restoring oxidative balance and mitigating inflammation. Moreover, CoNi-MOF promotes macrophage polarization from the pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype toward the pro-regenerative M2 phenotype. This pH-responsive enzymatic activity offers a self-adaptive therapeutic strategy, as validated by in vivo studies showing accelerated wound healing. This self-adaptive nanozyme platform integrates antibacterial, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory functions, offering a promising antibiotic-free treatment for drug-resistant bacterial wound infections.

candidates.title: Hypoxia-Tolerant Supramolecular Nanomicelles for Pyroptosis-Enhanced NIR-II Phototheranostics.
candidates.abstract: Tumor hypoxia, limited solid-tumor imaging, and insufficient systemic antitumor immunity remain major challenges to effective cancer phototheranostics. Here, a molecular conformation engineering strategy is developed to construct TBBP, which features a strengthened electron donor, a moderately twisted conformation, extended π-conjugation, and a robust molecular skeleton free of labile olefinic π-bridges. TBBP exhibits excellent photostability, broadband second near-infrared (1000-1600 nm) emission, and efficient photothermal conversion (42.17%). Supramolecular assembly with DSPE-PEG2000 affords stable TBBP nanomicelles, TBBP NPs, that selectively generate superoxide radicals (O2 -•) and retain potent Type I photodynamic therapy (PDT) activity under hypoxia. Photoactivated TBBP NPs further induce mitochondrial dysfunction and caspase-3/GSDME-mediated immunogenic pyroptosis, promoting dendritic cell maturation and CD8+ T cell infiltration. In a bilateral 4T1 tumor model, TBBP NPs enable high-contrast second near-infrared (NIR-II) imaging, while synergistic Type I PDT and photothermal therapy elicit systemic antitumor immunity, achieving 92.0% primary tumor inhibition and 47.7% distant tumor inhibition. This work establishes a molecular conformation engineering strategy and extends its functionality through supramolecular assembly, synergistically integrating NIR-II imaging, hypoxia-tolerant Type I phototherapy, and photoimmunotherapy, thereby providing a generalizable molecular design principle for the development of next-generation multifunctional organic phototheranostic agents.

candidates.title: Endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery for a somatotroph pituitary neuroendocrine tumor associated with an infraoptic course of the anterior cerebral artery: A case report.
candidates.abstract: Identifying cerebrovascular anomalies before neurosurgical procedures is essential to avoid intraoperative complications. An infraoptic course of the anterior cerebral artery (IOA) is a rare variant in which the anterior cerebral artery (ACA) arises near the ophthalmic artery and passes beneath the optic nerve. Despite numerous reports of cerebral aneurysms coexisting with IOA, reports of coexistence with brain tumors are extremely rare, and no studies have reported endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery (eTSS) performed for pituitary tumors. Failure to recognize this IOA anomaly preoperatively is critical owing to the risk of vascular injury. A 47-year-old man presented with acromegaly caused by a somatotroph pituitary neuroendocrine tumor. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a sellar-suprasellar mass, and biochemical testing confirmed excess growth hormone production. After lanreotide-induced tumor shrinkage, surgical treatment was planned. Preoperative MRI, computed tomography angiography, and three-dimensional (3D) fusion imaging demonstrated bilateral IOA and duplication of the left A1 segment. These images enabled a detailed assessment of the tumor, pituitary gland, and vascular anatomy, suggesting that extracapsular resection via eTSS can be safely performed. Intraoperatively, the IOA adhered to the dura as predicted. Total tumor resection was achieved without vascular injury. Postoperative MRI confirmed complete removal, and hormone levels were normalized. IOA is an exceptionally rare vascular anomaly, and unrecognized cases may lead to severe intraoperative complications. This case highlights the importance of meticulous preoperative imaging, particularly 3D fusion techniques, for IOA identification and safe eTSS planning for functional pituitary tumors.

candidates.title: Understanding the unfolded protein response in glioblastoma.
candidates.abstract: Glioblastoma is the most aggressive and lethal malignancy of the central nervous system and exhibits a complex interplay with endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress (ERS). The multifunctional ER is the primary site of the unfolded protein response (UPR), which is activated under conditions of ERS to enhance protein-folding capacity and promote cell survival. However, persistent ERS can trigger apoptosis. Despite extensive research over the past decades, the mechanistic insights into the impact of ERS and the UPR on glioblastoma pathogenesis and progression remain unclear. The UPR operates through three canonical signaling pathways: inositol-requiring enzyme 1 (IRE1), PKR-like ER kinase (PERK, also known as EIF2AK3) and activating transcription factor 6 (ATF6). These pathways regulate glioblastoma development through both independent and synergistic mechanisms. In this Review, we discuss the current state of research on the role of the UPR in glioblastoma and delineate the distinct mechanisms of each signaling pathway. Furthermore, we evaluate the challenges associated with UPR-targeting therapeutic agents and propose possible treatment strategies to leverage the regulatory mechanisms of the different UPR pathways to overcome these limitations.

candidates.title: Endocrine dysfunctions in patients with beta thalassemia major: a single-center retrospective study from Basrah.
candidates.abstract: The management of patients with beta thalassemia major (BTH) involves regular blood transfusions which are associated with iron overload. This may result in various endocrine dysfunctions (EDs). This study aimed to assess the obesrved frequency of different EDs in patients with transfusion-dependent BTH. A retrospective study that included 496 patients with BTH who were referred from the Basra Center for hereditary blood diseases to Faiha Specialized Diabetes, Endocrine and Metabolsim Center for endocrine-related complaints and underwent detailed endocrine assessments from Jan 2010 to Dec 2023. The mean presentation age for endocrine evaluation was 13.6 ± 6.5 years with no difference between male and female. The commonest clinical presentations of BTH patients in our center were short stature 65.5%, amenorrhea 16.4, hyperglycemia 13.7%, delayed puberty 13.3, and hypocalcemia 5.2%. The proportion patients with ED was 16.8%. The most frequent EDs were growth hormone deficiency (GHD) 6.0%, diabetes mellitus (DM) 4.9%, hypogonadism 4.5%, hypothyroidism 3.2%. Within those patients, 78.7% had single ED, 16.5% had two EDs and 4.8% had three or more EDs. EDs were observed among patients with BTH. The commonest EDs were GHD, DM, and hypogonadism. We recommend regular and timely surveillance using both clinical and hormonal assessment in patients with BTH.

candidates.title: Pertrochanteric fracture in case of Sheehan syndrome: A rare case report.
candidates.abstract: Sheehan's syndrome is caused by ischemic necrosis of the pituitary gland following hypo-perfusion to the pituitary gland. The prevalence is around 3.2% in women <40 years of age and is relatively common in developing countries. The diagnosis is made with the help of a suggestive obstetric history, clinical manifestations, laboratory findings of reduced hormone levels, and pertinent radiological features. The treatment is to replace the patient with deficient hormones and prevent the complications associated with it. We present the management of a patient with Sheehan's syndrome with pertrochanteric fracture due to the rarity of its presentation. The patient underwent the insertion of a proximal femur nail under closed reduction and achieved optimum results post operatively. As such no case reports with these findings have been documented in the literature or online sources.
